rules.title: Source of Income Discrimination Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to a tenant or treat them differently because of how they pay rent, including housing vouchers, rental assistance, disability benefits, or wages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing providers in California renting residential units.
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: Limits on Use of Criminal History in Tenant Screening
rules.requirement: Landlords may consider criminal history but cannot use arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, juvenile records, or blanket bans on all applicants with criminal history; any denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy suitability.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing providers screening rental applicants in California.
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
